key_concepts: Acceleration is the rate of change of an object's velocity
Acceleration is calculated as change in velocity divided by time
Acceleration can involve speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction
An object changing direction at constant speed is still accelerating
Negative acceleration or deceleration occurs when an object slows down
Uniform acceleration means equal changes in velocity in equal time intervals
Non-uniform acceleration means unequal changes in velocity over time
Forces such as pressing the pedal, braking, or turning cause acceleration
Acceleration problems can be solved for acceleration, time, or final velocity
Common units for acceleration are meters per second squared
